topics.title: Child development
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to state the basic needs of babies, explain how to prepare baby food, list common baby foods, and demonstrate the care of babies.

Introduction:
Last term we learned about family planning and pregnancy. Today we will focus on caring for babies after birth, which is important for every family member.

Content:
The care of babies includes feeding, bathing, changing diapers, and keeping them clean and warm. Baby food should be nutritious and easy to digest. Common Nigerian baby foods include pap (ogi), yam porridge, and mashed ripe plantain. To make pap, you mix the dry ogi with cold water, then add boiling water while stirring continuously until it thickens. Always test the temperature before giving to babies to avoid burns.

Class activity:
Students will work in groups to prepare a simple baby food using local ingredients like ripe plantain or yam.

Evaluation questions:
1. What are the three basic needs of a baby?
2. List two common Nigerian baby foods.
3. Why is it important to test baby food temperature?
4. How would you prepare ogi for a baby?

Summary:
Proper care and nutrition are essential for healthy baby development, and every student should know these basic skills.

topics.title: Housing the family
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify different types of houses, explain the importance of ventilation, and suggest ways to improve house ventilation.

Introduction:
Last week we discussed child development. Today we will learn about housing which provides shelter for families, just as a mother's womb protects a baby.

Content:
Types of houses in Nigeria include bungalows, flats, face-me-I-face-you, and mud houses. Ventilation is the circulation of fresh air in a house. Good ventilation prevents the spread of diseases, reduces heat, and removes bad smells. Houses in hot areas like Nigeria need good cross-ventilation. Windows, doors, and vents should be placed to allow air flow. In traditional Nigerian houses, we have high ceilings and large windows for natural ventilation.

Class activity:
Students will draw their ideal house showing proper ventilation features.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name three types of houses found in Nigeria.
2. Why is ventilation important in housing?
3. What features should a house have for good ventilation?
4. How does climate affect housing design in Nigeria?

Summary:
Good housing with proper ventilation is essential for the health and comfort of every family.

topics.title: Interior decoration
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain how colours affect a room, list principles of flower arrangement, and decorate a corner of the classroom.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about housing the family. Today we will focus on making our homes beautiful through interior decoration, which makes living spaces more pleasant.

Content:
Colours affect our mood - blue is calming, yellow is cheerful, and green is refreshing. In Nigerian homes, we often use bright colours to reflect our vibrant culture. Flower arrangement follows principles like balance, proportion, and harmony. Common Nigerian flowers for decoration include hibiscus, bougainvillea, and orchids. When arranging flowers, use a suitable container, trim stems at an angle, and arrange flowers of different heights. For a corner decoration, select a focal point, add plants, use colourful fabrics, and ensure proper lighting.

Class activity:
Students will decorate a corner of the classroom using available materials and principles learned.

Evaluation questions:
1. How do different colours affect a room's atmosphere?
2. What are the three principles of flower arrangement?
3. Name two Nigerian flowers used for decoration.
4. Why is lighting important in interior decoration?

Summary:
Good interior decoration creates a beautiful and comfortable living space that reflects our personal style and cultural heritage.

topics.title: Laundry work
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify different types of stains, explain methods of stain removal, and demonstrate stain removal on a fabric.

Introduction:
Last term we learned about textiles. Today we will focus on laundry work, which is essential for keeping our clothes clean and looking good, especially in our dusty Nigerian environment.

Content:
Stains are marks on fabrics caused by substances like oil, ink, or food. Common stains in Nigeria include palm oil, groundnut oil, and red oil from stew. Different stains need different removal methods. For oil stains, apply chalk or soap before washing. For ink stains, use milk or lemon juice. For food stains, soak in warm soapy water. Always test stain removers on a hidden area first. When removing stains, work from the outside to prevent spreading. After treatment, wash the garment as usual.

Class activity:
Students will practice removing different types of stains on fabric samples using appropriate methods.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name three common types of stains found in Nigerian homes.
2. What is the first step in treating any stain?
3. How would you remove an oil stain from a shirt?
4. Why should you test stain removers on hidden fabric areas?

Summary:
Proper stain removal techniques help maintain the quality and appearance of our clothes, making them last longer.

topics.title: Textiles
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to classify different types of fibres, explain their characteristics, and perform a simple fabric test.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about laundry work. Today we will study textiles, which are the materials we use to make our clothes, an important part of our daily lives in Nigeria.

Content:
Fibres are thin threads used to make fabrics. They are natural or synthetic. Natural fibres come from plants like cotton, linen, and hemp, or animals like wool and silk. Synthetic fibres are made in factories, like polyester and nylon. Cotton is common in Nigeria because it is breathable and absorbs sweat. Wool is warm but not suitable for our hot climate. To test fabrics, check if they burn - natural fibres smell like burning paper, while synthetic ones melt and smell like chemicals. You can also test by stretching or feeling the texture.

Class activity:
Students will test different fabric samples to identify their fibre types using various methods.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is the difference between natural and synthetic fibres?
2. Name two natural fibres commonly used in Nigeria.
3. How can you test if a fabric is natural or synthetic?
4. Why is cotton popular in Nigerian clothing?

Summary:
Understanding different textiles helps us choose appropriate fabrics for our clothing based on climate and purpose.

topics.title: Clothing repair
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify common clothing damages, explain basic mending techniques, and repair a simple garment.

Introduction:
Last week we studied different textiles. Today we will learn clothing repair, which is an important skill in Nigeria to make our clothes last longer and save money.

Content:
Common clothing damages include torn seams, loose buttons, and small holes. To mend a seam, use a needle and thread to stitch along the original line. For buttons, choose a matching thread, make a small knot, and stitch securely through the fabric. To patch a small hole, cut a piece of matching fabric slightly larger than the hole, place it under the hole, and stitch around the edges. In Nigeria, we often use durable threads and needles for repairs. Always mend clothes as soon as damage occurs to prevent further tearing.

Class activity:
Students will bring an item of clothing with minor damage and practice mending it using appropriate techniques.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name three common types of clothing damage.
2. What equipment is needed for basic clothing repair?
3. Describe how to replace a button securely.
4. Why is it important to mend clothes promptly?

Summary:
Basic clothing repair skills help maintain our garments, save money, and reduce waste in our communities.

topics.title: Personal finance
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to create a pocket money plan, explain the importance of saving, and maintain a simple savings record.

Introduction:
Last term we learned about food hygiene. Today we will discuss personal finance, which is important for managing the pocket money many of you receive from parents.

Content:
Pocket money planning involves allocating money for different needs like school materials, transport, and snacks. In Nigeria, pocket money is often given in naira coins and notes. Saving means keeping some money for future needs. A savings book helps track money saved and spent. To save effectively, set a goal, save regularly, and avoid unnecessary spending. Many Nigerian students save for textbooks, school fees, or personal items. You can save at home in a safe place or with a trusted adult. Remember, small savings grow over time.

Class activity:
Students will create a one-week pocket money plan showing how they would allocate #500.

Evaluation questions:
1. Why is planning pocket money important?
2. What are three common uses of pocket money in Nigeria?
3. How does a savings book help with money management?
4. What is one benefit of regular saving?

Summary:
Good financial habits learned early help ensure financial security and responsible money management in the future.

topics.title: Food hygiene
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to list safe cooking habits, explain kitchen hygiene practices, and conduct a kitchen inspection.

Introduction:
Last week we discussed personal finance. Today we will focus on food hygiene, which is crucial for preventing diseases in our homes and communities across Nigeria.

Content:
Safe cooking habits include washing hands before cooking, using clean utensils, and cooking food thoroughly. Kitchen hygiene involves keeping surfaces clean, storing food properly, and disposing of waste correctly. In Nigeria's hot climate, food spoils quickly, so proper storage is essential. Always cover food to prevent contamination, keep raw and cooked food separate, and clean cooking areas regularly. Harmful bacteria like E. coli can cause serious illness. When inspecting a kitchen, check for cleanliness, food storage, pest control, and waste management.

Class activity:
Students will inspect the school kitchen or a model kitchen, identifying areas of improvement in food hygiene.

Evaluation questions:
1. List three safe cooking habits.
2. Why is kitchen hygiene important in Nigeria's climate?
3. What should you check during a kitchen inspection?
4. How does proper food storage prevent illness?

Summary:
Maintaining food hygiene is essential for preventing foodborne diseases and ensuring the health of our families.

topics.title: Entertainment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to plan elements of a small party, organize entertainment activities, and host a simple event.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about food hygiene. Today we will discuss entertainment, which brings families and friends together in joyful gatherings, an important part of Nigerian culture.

Content:
Planning a small party involves deciding on the number of guests, venue, food, and activities. Nigerian parties often include local foods like jollof rice, moi moi, and puff-puff. Entertainment can be music, games, or storytelling. Traditional Nigerian entertainment includes drumming, dancing, and folk tales. When hosting, welcome guests warmly, serve food promptly, and ensure everyone is included. Budgeting is important - allocate money for food, drinks, and decorations. Remember to consider cultural preferences and dietary restrictions of guests.

Class activity:
Students will work in groups to plan a mini-party within a budget of #2000, including menu and activities.

Evaluation questions:
1. What are three important elements to consider when planning a party?
2. Name two traditional Nigerian entertainment forms.
3. Why is budgeting important for party planning?
4. How should a host make all guests feel welcome?

Summary:
Proper party planning and hosting create memorable experiences that strengthen relationships within our communities.

topics.title: Revision and BECE practice
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to answer past examination questions, identify common mistakes, and apply knowledge from previous topics.

Introduction:
Throughout this term, we have covered various topics in Home Economics. Today we will revise these topics and practice BECE examination questions to prepare for your final exams.

Content:
Revision involves going over key points from each topic we studied. Important areas include child care, housing, textiles, laundry, food hygiene, and personal finance. BECE questions often test both knowledge and application skills. When answering questions, read carefully, plan your response, and provide specific examples. Common mistakes include not following instructions, not answering all parts of questions, and not relating answers to Nigerian contexts. Practice time management during exams to ensure you complete all questions.

Class activity:
Students will work in pairs to answer past BECE questions and then discuss their answers with the class.

Evaluation questions:
1. Explain two important aspects of food hygiene.
2. How would you remove palm oil stain from a shirt?
3. Why is good ventilation important in housing?
4. Describe one method of saving money effectively.
5. What factors should be considered when planning a party?

Summary:
Regular practice of past questions helps build confidence and improves performance in examinations.
